Throughout this section, let $\cV$ be a \emph{monoidal bicategory}. In particular, we can choose $\cV$ to be a one-object \emph{algebraic tricategory} in the sense of \cite{gurski2006tricat, gurski2013tricatcoh}, and shall denote the relevant data of the monoidal bicategory $\cV$ as $(\cV, \otimes, I, a_{\cV}, a_{\cV}^{-1},\lambda_{\cV},\lambda_{\cV}^{-1},\rho_{\cV},\rho_{\cV}^{-1})$, omitting any labeling of the $2$-cell data. Thus, for simplicity, one may also consider $\cV$ as a $\nCat{1}$-enriched monoidal category. Under this consideration, all of the forthcoming coherence diagram are supposed to be read inside the cubical tricategory $\st\cV$. In particular, we must incorporate the fact that $\otimes$ is a pseudofunctor with non-trivial coherence constraints. Thus, for instance, $a \otimes 1$ (when seen in $\st\cV$) is supposed to be the image of $a$ combined with appropriate coherence data under the pseudofunctor $\cV \rightarrow \cV \times * \xrightarrow{1 \times M} \cV \times \cV \xrightarrow{\otimes} \cV$. Some similar or same diagrams are also available in \cite{yau2024bimodcats} for the case of $\nCat{1}$-enriched categories. More generally, some of these diagrams can be seen as one object versions of \cite[Defs.~3.2, 3.3, and 3.4]{gurski2014itericon}.

\subsection{Hexagon identities}\label{app:hexagon}

We assume that we have a suitable definition of a braided monoidal bicategory in sense of being a one object tricategory equipped with some coherent braiding adjoint equivalence. In particular, $\cV$ is a braided monoidal bicategory if it is a monoidal bicategory equipped with a family of adjoint equivalences $b_{x,y} : X \otimes Y \leftrightarrow Y \otimes X : b_{x,y}^{-1}$ that behaves as the braiding. The details are ultimately irrelevant for us but can be found carefully constructed in \cite{gurski2011monbicat}. Other relevant sources include \cite{yau2cat2021,pries2011monbicat}.

	\arrow["{b_{M,M \otimes M}}", from=1-2, to=1-4]
